grades.quote: If no data is available, a read on a pipe waits for either data to be written or for all file descriptors referring to the write end to be closed; in the latter case, read will return 0, just as if the end of a data file had been reached.
grades.reason: Directly explains why a pipe read does not see EOF: read returns 0 only when all write-end descriptors are closed. It also says the child (and parent) must close unused write ends, or the reader never sees end-of-file. This is the usual cause of the reported symptom.
Covers fork/exec/waitpid and zombie processes. It says nothing about pipes or EOF on pipe reads, so it doesn't help diagnose the problem.
An exercise about ping-ponging a byte over pipes. It has no information on EOF behavior or on diagnosing a reader that never sees EOF.
Describes a shell pipeline and the pipe's bounded buffer. It does not discuss EOF or closing write ends, so it doesn't address the problem.
